definition: The DME box in the aircraft. It sends short radio questions to the ground station and times how long the answers take.
The ground part of a DME. It listens for questions from aircraft, waits a fixed time and answers each one.
Two short radio pulses a fixed time apart. DME questions and answers are pulse pairs; the spacing tells the receiver which channel mode (X or Y) it is.
The fixed wait between the ground station hearing a question and sending its answer: 50 microseconds on X channels, 56 on Y channels. The aircraft subtracts it before working out the distance.
One of 252 DME channels: numbers 1 to 126, each in an X and a Y version. X and Y use different pulse spacings and reply delays, so two stations can share nearby frequencies.
Each VOR or ILS frequency belongs to exactly one DME channel. Tuning the VOR or ILS automatically tunes its DME, for example 108.00 MHz with channel 17X.
Spacing the questions randomly instead of evenly. Answers to your own questions then keep coming back at the same delay, while everyone else's answers land at random times.
Random pulse pairs a DME ground station sends when few aircraft are asking, so its transmitter and the aircraft receivers keep working steadily.
How the DME in the aircraft finds its answers. While searching it asks fast and looks for a delay where answers keep lining up. Once it finds one it tracks it and asks more slowly.
When the answers stop for a moment, the DME keeps showing its last distance for a few seconds before it gives up and starts searching again.
How fast the DME distance is changing. It equals the real groundspeed only when flying straight toward or away from the station.
The share of an aircraft's questions that get an answer from the ground station. It falls when the station is very busy.
A short moment after each answer (about 60 microseconds) when the ground station cannot hear new questions.
More aircraft asking than the ground station can answer. It then turns down its receiver sensitivity so it keeps answering the closest aircraft, and the farthest ones lose their answers.
